The is_lot / is_bulk_or_sealed gates stay ON (the plain 'Set' passes them, while lots/bundles/playsets are rejected). require = one piece + 3rd/third anniv + 'set' (excludes 1st/2nd anniversary and singles that say 'card' not 'set'). exclude 'campaign'/'treasure' drops the separate '3rd Anniversary Treasure Campaign Promo Collection' (~$26-80); 'playset' drops multi-single playsets. min_price 500 cuts the cheap no-number singles/accessories (alt-art/leader singles $100-420, deck/storage box, guide book) — the real sealed set is ~$620-2000. language 'english' drops the Japanese version. watches.name: Psyduck #20 WOTC Black Star Promo (English, 2000)
watches._note: Pokemon, English vintage (WOTC Black Star Promo #20 / 20/53, Pokemon League release 2000, non-holo, illus. Kagemaru Himeno). Bare '20' is UNSAFE: years 2000/2019/2025 all normalize to CONTAIN '20', and modern Psyduck promos (2025 Mega Evolution #007, 2019 Detective Pikachu SM199) ALSO say 'Black Star Promo', so they'd match psyduck+blackstar+20 via the year. Dual defense: the clean self-sufficient '20/53'->'2053' signature, plus match_any covering the other real seller forms (blackstar+20; WOTC-Promo 'wotcp'+20; Pokemon-League+20 for terse 'BS #20' titles with no black-star/wotc token; TCGplayer 'Promo Regular'+20) guarded by a modern-marker exclude wall (mega evolution/mep/enme/007/sm199/detective/scarlet/226-217/039-217/prize pack/van gogh/cosmos). Foreign WOTC #20 prints keep the English name 'Psyduck' but title in German/French ('Pokemon Liga/Ligue') or name the language -> excluded (german/french/italian/spanish/portuguese/dutch/liga/ligue), the Espeon 1/75 precedent. Designed + adversarially verified by a 3-agent workflow (~300 live listings) then independently re-scraped (159 listings: 129 real #20 matched, 9 correctly excluded [modern MEP/SM199/Portuguese], 0 real #20 wrongly killed); FN=0 FP=0 on a 41-TRUE/37-FALSE battery. Documented edges: (a) a terse modern listing with only a bare year and no set marker could leak; (b) a real #20 slab whose CERT number happens to contain '007' would be missed — unobserved in live data (mid-value card, cert# rarely in title).
